newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X CEO says no Busang deal signed yet.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X CEO says no Busang deal signed yet.

text.p: The chief executive officer of Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Friday that his company has not yet signed any agreements for its giant Busang gold project in Indonesia.
"If we had signed a memorandum of understanding with any company, we would have to announce it, we would have to put out a press release," David Walsh said in a phone interview.

He said Bre-X will respond to the Indonesian government by Monday on its request that Bre-X form a deal with its Indonesian partners. But before Bre-X announces any deals, it must consult with its financial advisers, Walsh said.
"J.P. Morgan must provide a fairness opinion on any transaction with any company," he said.

Walsh would not confirm or deny reports his company was ready to do a deal involving New Orleans-based Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc. And he would not say whether Barrick Gold Corp, long considered to be the front runner in negotiations for Busang, was still in the running. "Don't ask me who we're talking to or not talking to," he said.
He said investors should expect a company announcement next week, but likely after Monday, a U.S. market holiday.
Sources close to the deal said the Indonesian government would likely hold off announcing anything until Tuesday, following which the companies involved would make their own announcements.
"I would say things will be concluded fairly shortly," Walsh said.
He said his financial advisers were prepared to react quickly after hearing from the Indonesian government.
"We're crunching out various scenarios on a regular basis so they can respond very quickly," Walsh said.
He said his company was reluctant to respond to market speculation about the outcome of negotiations, but agreed to be interviewed in order to console regulatory authorities.
A spokeswoman for Freeport would not comment on speculation the company was interested in Busang. She said her company would not comment until the Indonesian government had made an announcement.
